title: Pitch vs Tempo: What to Change for Music Practice
description: Pitch changes how high or low notes sound; tempo changes how fast the beat moves.
direct: Pitch changes how high or low notes sound; tempo changes how fast the beat moves. For music practice, change pitch to suit a comfortable key and tempo to give yourself more time to learn a passage. Neither operation guarantees an artifact-free recording.
figureAlt: Guitar and metronome distinguish pitch, or note height, from tempo, or beat speed.

cards.choice.heading: Choose the change you need
cards.choice.body: A song that is too high calls for a pitch adjustment. A passage that is too fast calls for a tempo adjustment. Changing one does not mean the other must change.
sections.explain.heading: Why voices can sound unnatural
sections.explain.body: A mixed recording contains voices, instruments and transients together. Processing the complete mix can change vocal character or introduce audible artifacts. A pitch tool is not proof of formant correction, vocal separation or studio-quality transposition. Those advanced capabilities are not claimed here.
sections.practice.heading: Keep a useful reference
sections.practice.body: Our app, developed by Space Sheep Studio, lists pitch and tempo changes for practice in its current iPhone release. Export tools require Pro. Use a normal-speed original alongside the practice copy so you can check the intended rhythm. Streaming-service playback is not the same as an importable audio file; use an accessible local source.
